note: PLACEHOLDER. Every params object here validates against the published top_community_issues manifest input_schema (additionalProperties: false, $refs inlined the way publish_experiments.py inlines them), and every value is plausible, but nobody has dispatched one. So a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the agent. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open — do not read the shortfall as a decision. {judgeOrgSlug} is not a value: they are substituted at dispatch time from the identifiers judgeIdentifiers.ts resolves once per sweep, and assertNoPlaceholders refuses the whole list before the first dispatch if a sweep did not supply one. For this agent the token resolves to the fixed judge-fixture slug rather than the per-sweep one, because it reads gp-api: step 2 reads the current issue feed with GET_community_issues scoped to that organization so carried issues keep their existing IDs. The dispatch names the seeded fixture account (scripts/seed-judge-fixture.ts, judgeFixtureIdentity.ts), so that read returns the fixture's feed: the same office-agnostic issues for every case and on both arms. The organization is therefore the one axis this list cannot vary. Varied along: district geometry, which is what decides whether the L2 predicate is a ward string, a bare district number or a whole jurisdiction — City_Ward, City_Council_Commissioner_District, City, County_Commissioner_District and Borough_Ward each appear; district population, where a Minneapolis ward and a Bellefonte borough ward are two orders of magnitude of voter file rows and of how much local news exists to attach to a ranked issue; urban against rural; and one case with no L2 pair at all, which is the documented fallback to state scope and the only way the lean annotation's absence gets exercised. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named and every URL is under example.org. States, cities, office titles and L2 voter file column names are real. THE GEOGRAPHY IS CARRIED BY THE OTHER PARAMS. {judgeOrgSlug} resolves to judge-fixture for every case, while each case's own state/office/district_descriptor names somewhere else. That is not a mismatch to fix in this file: the dispatch message's organization_slug, not this param, is what the broker sends gp-api, and it is the same judge-fixture slug. Both arms receive the identical value and read the identical feed, so the comparison is unaffected.
